::: {#def-automatic-differentiation}

#### Automatic differentiation (autodiff)

**Automatic differentiation**, also called **autodiff**, computes the derivatives of a function that is given as code,
by applying the chain rule to the elementary operations the code performs as it runs
[@goodfellow2016deep, section 6.5; @paszke2019pytorch].

PyTorch's automatic differentiation is called autograd.
The result is the exact derivative of the operations the code performs, up to floating-point rounding.
Automatic differentiation is neither symbolic differentiation,
which manipulates a formula for the function,
nor numerical differentiation,
which approximates a derivative from the function's values at nearby points.
lds's [backpropagation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html) chapter derives by hand the derivatives that autodiff computes for a neural network.

:::
